Working on setting up a ~48 plant indoor drip feed, will post pictures soon. what are you working on?
Share your creative solutions to medium to large scale irrigation dilemas
What's your reasoning behind drip feed? Drain to waste, recirculating or just transpiration governed?

Well, its a soil system, and drip feed seemed easiest although not my first choice. I was thinking drain to waste but Im really still thinking it through. Thats why I started this post, Here's my parameters.. ~48 plants indoor (warehouse) in soil-less mixture, all fed from 2 55 gallon drums. When I say drip system, I dont mean a true drip, I mean it would only run for ~15 minutes every other day to soak the soil. I'm interested to hear what you think, I know thats not much information to work off, but what kind of irrigation would you recommend

15 minutes every other day doesn't sound like enough, but I have no experience with that either. Soil-less should have a high drain rate, like Coco, which should allow watering more frequently. Probably a few times a day.

If you look at the crap that some Licensed Producers set up, who tend to produce a lot of garbage, they work with sea of greens and don't leave much volume for root growth. I've seen real spaghetti like messes of networked drip lines that just looks like a massive clusterfuck and don't think they care about even watering or clogging. It's probably more of a make shift flood table that seems to drain only through transpiration. Which is lazy and likely prone to problems that will have them reliant on chemicals to counteract their poor planning, or end up being a lot more work in the end.

I've heard of very elaborate setups that just seem especially confused. For example, a "recirculating" drip feed that's drain to waste. Usually "drip" and "circulating" are at odds.

But actually wasting it isn't that great because it's not necessarily spent in one pass, and when a lot of setups drain to waste it pollutes the environment/water supply. I think that's why the Dutch developed new techniques to recirculate and you might look into the dutch bucket method, which just seems to be a form of recirculating water culture which isn't that optimal.

Start up costs for what you describe probably comes in at the lower end of the spectrum based on its initial simplicity but that might cost you in other ways. Like having to turn over your soil-less mix.

What you describe with soil-less is already hydroponics. It's just not the most efficient form. So it depends what your objective is as well. Mono-cropping? Small sea of green or spread out and hoping for large plants?

Drip feeding from the top probably isn't so ideal either. It's not very even, you'll get salt concentrating and pH issues.

Elaborate black market grows seemed to love the drip feed/top fed setups and that has carried over to shit holes like Tweed. Their advantage, I assume, was low cost, easy to tear down. Also somewhat modular. But in practice that seems to not be a big deal.

I'd prefer full hydroponics given their advantages. Full access to roots, maintaining the water is all that you have to do, and easier to automate to some degree or other. It is easier to get and maintain it absolutely right. With those conditions at all stable than growth rate is absurd.

Bioponic setups are the most efficient and ultimate that you can do.

When I was a kid, we didn't even have video games at home -- we had to go to an arcade and play games standing up, putting quarters into the game to keep it going.

Later, my family got a used Atari 2600 and all of the games were so excellent and so exciting, but in retrospect, they were just colored squares and simple programming, and we were all excited just to be able to interact with things on our television.

Soon after that, my babysitter who took care of me was angry because her son's ColecoVision basketball characters burned a pattern into her cathode ray tube television.

When I look at modern video games today, I am honestly astonished by how realistic the graphics are, by how lifelike the AI interactions are, and by the multitude of free-will choices I have in sandbox games.
